summary.business: Hindustan Unilever Limited is India's largest Fast-Moving Consumer Goods company, serving consumers for over 90 years across Home Care, Beauty & Wellbeing, Personal Care and Foods. It reaches consumers through one of the country's most extensive distribution networks, spanning over 9 million retail outlets across urban and rural India, and combines deep consumer insight with world-class R&D to drive category-shaping innovation and build iconic, market-leading brands.

currentContext.strengths: Extensive distribution network of 9 million+ retail outlets reaching 9 out of 10 Indian households, with a digitally-enabled retailer ecosystem (~1.4 Mn retailers onboarded on Shikhar)|Wide, resilient portfolio of 50 brands across 15 FMCG categories with stated market leadership across segments|Deep R&D and innovation capability (800+ scientists) augmented by AI/analytics across demand sensing, supply chain and marketing, including a new 'Liquids Lab of the Future' for faster time-to-market|Industry-leading corporate governance, strong balance sheet and robust cash generation
currentContext.strategies: Creating desire at scale through modern, youthful brands, strengthening future-ready marketing and channel moats, and accelerating market development across high-growth demand spaces|Personal Care doubling-down on fewer, bigger bets: premiumising bars through Dove and Pears, scaling bodywash as the next growth engine, dialling up freshness and whitening in Oral Care, and expanding roll-ons and deodorants|Foods pursuing four strategic big bets: Premiumise Tea and Coffee, Pivot to Lifestyle Nutrition, Build Kissan into a Mega Food Brand and Build Ready-To-Drink|Future-proofing the frontline engine across channels — general trade as the rural backbone, modern trade as the premiumisation engine, and accelerated investment in e-commerce and quick commerce|Social-first Demand Generation used across segments to deepen brand engagement and drive discovery/trial through digital and creator-led content|Serving differentiated consumer segments (Power Spenders, Premiumisers, Democratisers) by aligning brand investment, channel resources and innovation across the portfolio|Management describes a disciplined and disruptive savings culture pursuing buying, supply-chain and net-revenue-management efficiencies across the P&L, which are reinvested in brands, innovation and capability building. Capital is sharply allocated to growth-accretive opportunities through a rigorous, continuous portfolio reassessment blending acquisitions and divestments (demerger of Ice Cream, acquisition of OZiva and Minimalist, divestment of Nutritionalab stake). The Company states it remains committed to delivering superior shareholder returns through a combination of high-quality, profitable growth, disciplined capital allocation and dividend payouts, alongside structured investor engagement (one-on-one meetings, investor conferences, quarterly earnings calls) and a Stakeholder Relationship Committee overseeing shareholder concerns.
currentContext.expansion: The Company continues to step up its capex commitment, with the majority of spend directed towards capacity creation, productivity enhancements and innovation-led initiatives; one such example is a planned investment of up to Rs 2,000 crores over two years aimed at expanding capacity (in fast-growing premium categories across Beauty & Wellbeing and Home Care liquids, per the MD&A). During the year the Company completed the demerger of its Ice Cream business for greater strategic flexibility, completed the full acquisition of Zywie Ventures Private Limited (OZiva) to double down on Health & Wellbeing, and acquired a 90.5% stake in Uprising Science Private Limited (Minimalist) to strengthen its play in Masstige Beauty, while divesting its 19.8% stake in Nutritionalab Pvt. Ltd. as part of ongoing portfolio sharpening. A dedicated quick commerce organisation was also set up to capture rapid growth in instant delivery. Separately, BRSR disclosures note capex on environmental/social infrastructure projects including upgrading infrastructure, a Fire suppression system, Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD), an Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP), and energy-efficient systems such as magnetic chillers and heat pumps.
currentContext.mdna: Indian economy delivered real GDP growth of around 7.4% in FY26, supported by strengthening domestic demand, robust public investment and resilient macro fundamentals|FMCG sector in India showed gradually improving performance through FY26 on moderating inflation, demand recovery and improved consumer sentiment aided by policy measures|Rural markets began to show signs of revival following a favourable monsoon and improving agricultural activity, though recovery remained uneven and sensitive to food inflation|Urban demand remained steadier but showed periods of moderation linked to weaker consumption in select discretionary categories|Consumer behaviour shows value-seeking and selective premiumisation co-existing across categories, with e-commerce, quick commerce and modern trade outpacing general trade and reshaping discovery/purchasing patterns|Cost environment was divergent across commodities: tea prices deflated, palm oil stayed inflationary, crude oil turned inflationary late in the year, and Rupee depreciation intensified input cost pressure — prompting calibrated pricing actions|Foods business outlook: well-positioned to benefit from an improving macro-economic environment and structural demand tailwinds reshaping consumption in India

risks.note: Categorised by the Board as a Market, Economic and Operational Risk with an 'Increased' level of change. Geopolitical uncertainties, commodity volatility and supply-side shocks threaten service reliability, cost efficiency and business continuity across HUL's supply chain; the AR separately notes divergent commodity trends (tea deflation vs. inflationary palm oil and late-year crude spike) and Rupee depreciation intensifying input cost pressure. Mitigated via diversified/multi-geography sourcing, agile manufacturing and logistics technology, cost hedging and forward buying, and predictive supply-chain planning.

risks.risk: Competitive intensity and shifting brand preferences
risks.note: Categorised by the Board as a Market Risk with 'No change' in level. The FMCG market faces rapidly evolving consumer preferences (demographic shifts, health/wellness trends, sustainability awareness, digital influence) and new entrants with differing business models intensifying competition, requiring continual innovation and purpose-driven brand-building to defend market share. Mitigated through insight-led brand evolution, the SASSY innovation framework, purpose-driven storytelling, omnichannel engagement and category management.

one-line thesis: HUL delivered flat underlying sales growth in Q4FY26 due to transitory GST transition disruptions across 40% of its portfolio, but structural benefits from GST rate cuts to 5% and the upcoming Ice Cream demerger are set to unlock volume-led growth and margin expansion; the company is doubling down on premiumization, rural segmentation, and digital channels to drive sustainable long-term value.
financial scorecard: revenue: +2% UG (price-led); EBITDA/margin: 23.2% (-90 bps YoY); PAT (rptd): +4% (one-off tax benefit); PAT (normalized): -4%; order book: none; net debt: reduced post special dividend & Minimalist acquisition
guidance: revenue growth: H2 FY26 to outperform H1; margin: 22-23% (pre-demerger); order inflow: none; capex/commissioning: Ice Cream demerger completion by Dec 2025
segment / subsidiary detail: Home Care: mid-single digit UVG, flat USG due to crude deflation; Fabric Wash: double-digit volume growth in liquids; Personal Care: flat USG due to 90% portfolio GST transition; Skin Care: high-single digit growth; Foods: 3% USG; Beverages: double-digit growth; Ice Cream: declined due to monsoon + GST; Minimalist: double-digit growth; OZiva: triple-digit growth
growth verticals / optionality: Accelerating premiumization in soaps (Dove, Pears, Lux); scaling Beauty-from-within (OZiva, Horlicks Pro Fitness); expanding d-commerce & q-commerce; developing liquids penetration in Personal Care (under 2% in India); rural demand capture via radical consumer segmentation (Power Spenders, Premiumisers, Democratisers)
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin improved 130 bps QoQ; EBITDA margin diluted by 90 bps YoY due to +80 bps A&P investment; GST transition caused transitory trade support costs; commodity tailwinds (crude, tea) offset palm oil/SMP inflation; Ice Cream demerger to add 50-60 bps to reported margin from Dec 2025
capex / expansion: none specified; Ice Cream demerger is corporate action, not capex
capital allocation: Interim dividend of Rs 19/share (Rs 4,464 cr total); strategic M&A (Minimalist acquisition); focus on brand investment over buybacks; demerger of Ice Cream business to unlock shareholder value
risks & watch-items: Prolonged monsoon disrupting supply chains; GST transition lingering trade destocking until Nov 2025; consumer sentiment delay in pantry replenishment; competitive pricing pressure in Home Care; execution risk in rural channel revival
management quality / tone: Confident, transformational, and execution-focused; Priya Nair (new CEO) emphasized volume-led growth, radical segmentation, and premiumization; Ritesh Tiwari (outgoing CFO) conveyed strong institutional discipline; Niranjan Gupta (new CFO) brought credibility and stability; tone is optimistic on structural reforms and long-term demand
non-obvious takeaways: GST reform benefits are concentrated in 40% of portfolio (Skin Cleansing, Hair Care, Packaged Foods); rural demand revival is a hidden lever; HUL’s 80B annual consumer interactions enable hyper-targeted innovation; Ice Cream demerger timing aligns with festive season recovery

themes.title: Consumption revival & FMCG premiumization
themes.need: Rural recovery, GST 2.0 and premiumization still frame the theme, but Q1FY27 rewarded portfolio SHAPE over volume. TATACONSUM's growth businesses hit INR 1,300cr (+47%) and are now 36% of India - larger than either salt (>INR 1,000cr) or tea & coffee (INR 1,200cr), with Sampann +58%, RTD +41% and Capital Foods INR 232cr (+40%) - while India tea revenue fell 4% on +2% volume as lower tea costs were deliberately passed back (tea inflation is now running 7-10% with most buying still ahead, so that inverts next year). PGHH shows the margin route: FY26 sales roughly flat at ~INR 4,300cr but PAT +19% to ~INR 850cr and ~100bps of structural margin from INR 86cr of productivity savings, absorbing crude and resin each up 30-50% with no stock-outs. The cautionary tale is licensed brands - JYOTHYLAB lost the Pril and Fa licences when Henkel did not renew (all manufacturing and selling stopped 1-June; Pril was ~7-8% of revenue, ~INR 225-240cr) and has filed SIAC arbitration. MARICO/DABUR/GODREJCP/COLPAL/EMAMILTD ride distribution + premium mix; VBL on beverage route-to-market; BIKAJI/GOPAL/BECTORFOOD on branded snacks; ORKLAINDIA took a 4% blended price increase in Q4 plus premium mix to a 16.9% EBITDA margin.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull-through; rural volume recovery; festive/wedding restocking; commodity pass-back timing; JYOTHYLAB's ~7-8% revenue hole and the SIAC arbitration.
